title: 1971 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship
text:
{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | |year=1971| |dates=16 May – 5 September 1971 |teams=15 |image=| |team=Tipperary | |titles=22nd | |captain=[[Tadhg O'Connor]]| |manager= |team2= Kilkenny | |captain2=[[Pat Henderson (hurler)|Pat Henderson]] |munster= Tipperary | |leinster=Kilkenny| |ulster=| |connacht=| |poty= [[Michael Keating (hurler)|Michael 'Babs' Keating]]| |topscorer= [[Eddie Keher]] (4–43) |matches=14| |totalgoals= |totalpoints= |previous=[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1970|1970]] |next=[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1972|1972]] }} The '''1971 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 84th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter county|inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. The championship began on 16 May 1971 and ended on 5 September 1971. [[Cork GAA|Cork]] were the [[1970 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]] but were defeated by [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] in the [[#Munster semi-finals|Munster semi-final]].{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30994055.html|title=Plenty of discoveries to be made in deep dive of GAA digital archive|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=15 April 2020|accessdate=14 May 2023|first=John|last=Fogarty}}{{cite news|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-40252727.html|title=Reeling on the banks of the Lee: History of Cork sports 1970 to 1974|publisher=Echo Live|date=31 March 2021|accessdate=14 May 2023|first=Derek|last=Daly}}{{cite news|url=https://www.irishpost.com/sport/clash-of-the-ash-the-greatest-hurlers-of-the-1970s-200485|title=CLASH OF THE ASH: The greatest hurlers of the 1970s|publisher=The Irish Post|date=2 January 2021|accessdate=14 May 2023|first=Henry|last=Wymbs}} [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]], who won the [[All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship]] in 1970, were promoted to the senior championship after a long absence.{{cite news|url=https://thesaffrongael.com/2020/10/04/fifty-golden-years-ago-antrim-hurlers-made-a-breakthrough/|title=Fifty golden years ago today Antrim hurlers made the breakthrough|publisher=The Saffron Gael|date=4 October 2020|accessdate=14 May 2023|first=|last=}} The [[#All-Ireland final|All-Ireland final]] was played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 5 September 1971 between [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] and [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]], in what was their 16th championship meeting overall and a first meeting in the All-Ireland final [[1967 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|four years]]. Tipperary won the match by 5–17 to 5–14 to claim their 22nd All-Ireland title overall and a first title in [[1965 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|six years]].{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20418952.html|title=When Tipp edged Keher-inspired Kilkenny in 10-goal final thriller|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=2 September 2016|accessdate=18 February 2026|first=Peter|last=McNamara}}{{cite news|url=https://www.tipperarylive.ie/news/sport/621393/tipperary-s-all-ireland-success-in-1971-coincided-with-abolition-of-the-ludicrous-ban.html|title=Tipperary's All-Ireland success in 1971 coincided with abolition of the ludicrous Ban|publisher=Tipperary Live|date=5 April 2021|accessdate=18 February 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://www.the42.ie/action-replay-reeling-in-the-championships-of-yesteryear-135643-May2011/|title=Action replay: Reeling in the championships of yesteryear|publisher=The 42|date=13 May 2011|accessdate=18 February 2026|first=|last=}} Kilkenny's [[Eddie Keher]] was the championship's [[#Top scorers|top scorer]] with 4–43. Tipperary's [[Babs Keating|Michael 'Babs' Keating]] was the choice for [[Texaco Hurler of the Year]].{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40239770.html|title=Dry balls and stolen boots: Michael 'Babs' Keating relives finest hour in Tipperary jersey|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=8 March 2021|accessdate=19 May 2023|first=|last=}} ==The championship== ===Participating counties=== {| class="wikitable" |- !rowspan="2"|Province !rowspan="2"|County !colspan="3"|Most recent success |- !All-Ireland !Provincial |- |'''[[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster]]''' |[[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] |1938 |1961 |- | |[[Kildare GAA|Kildare]] | | |- | |[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] |1969 |1969 |- | |[[Laois GAA|Laois]] |1915 |1949 |- | |[[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] | | |- | |[[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] | | |- | |[[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] |1968 |1970 |- |'''[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]]''' |[[Clare GAA|Clare]] |1914 |1932 |- | |[[Cork GAA|Cork]] |1970 |1970 |- | |[[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] |1940 |1955 |- | |[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] |1965 |1968 |- | |[[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] |1959 |1963 |- |'''[[Connacht Senior Hurling Championship|Connacht]]''' |[[Galway GAA|Galway]] |1923 |1922 |- |'''[[Ulster Senior Hurling Championship|Ulster]]''' |[[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] | |1946 |- |'''[[Britain GAA|Britain]]''' |[[London GAA|London]] |1901 | |} ===Format=== The All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship of 1971 was run on a provincial basis as usual. It was a [[knockout tournament]] with pairings drawn at random in the respective provinces – there were no [[Single-elimination tournament#Seeding|seeds]]. Each match was played as a single leg. If a match was drawn there was a replay. If both sides were still level at the end of that game another replay had to take place. ====Munster Championship==== ''Quarter-final:'' (1 match) This was a single match between the first two teams drawn from the province of Munster. ''Semi-finals:'' (2 matches) The winner of the lone quarter-final joined the other three Munster teams to make up the semi-final pairings. ''Final:'' (1 match) The winner of the two semi-finals contested this game. ====Leinster Championship==== ''First round:'' (1 match) This was a single match between two of the 'weaker' teams drawn from the province of Leinster. ''Quarter-finals:'' (2 matches) The winner of the first-round game joined three other Leinster teams to make up the two quarter-final pairings. ''Semi-finals:'' (2 matches) The winners of the two quarter-finals joined Kilkenny and Wexford, who received a bye to this stage, to make up the semi-final pairings. ''Final:'' (1 match) The winner of the two semi-finals contested this game. ====All-Ireland Championship==== ''Quarter-final:'' (1 match) This was a single match between Antrim and Galway, two teams who faced no competition in their respective provinces. ''Semi-finals:'' (2 matches) The winner of the lone quarter-final joined London and the Munster and Leinster champions to make up the semi-final pairings. The provincial champions were drawn in opposite semi-finals. ''Final:'' (1 match) The winner of the two semi-finals contested this game. ==Provincial championships== ===[[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]]=== '''First round'''{{football box | date = 16 May 1971

Some years later, it was revealed that RTÉ had recorded over its only copy of archive footage of the game, due to a shortage of blank cassette tape. * Kilkenny's [[Eddie Keher]] set a new scoring record in an All-Ireland final.
